outcome: Hemorrhage-related morbidity (defined as intraoperative or postoperative red blood cell transfusion or the need for additional surgical interventions including uterine artery ligation, hypogastric artery ligation, or peripartum hysterectomy for atony)
cohort: Women who underwent cesarean delivery and received either methylergonovine or carboprost for refractory uterine atony
finding: In women who received second-line uterotonics for refractory uterine atony at cesarean delivery, methylergonovine was associated with a lower risk of hemorrhage-related morbidity compared to carboprost.
mod_finding: This study compared methylergonovine and carboprost for refractory uterine atony during cesarean delivery and found that methylergonovine was associated with a lower risk of hemorrhage-related morbidity.
